newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Acer says countersuing Lucent in patent row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Acer says countersuing Lucent in patent row.

text.p: Taiwan computer giant Acer Inc said on Friday it was countersuing U.S. company Lucent Technologies in a dispute over patent infringement allegations.

Acer general counsel and legal department chief Robert Chen told Reuters by telephone that the countersuit was being filed in the same U.S. district court in Delaware where Lucent filed its suit against Acer and its U.S. subsidiaries.
"We will file a reply to the Lucent suit saying we are confident that we have never infringed on Lucent's patents," Chen said from his Taipei office.
"Furthermore, we will countersue Lucent, alleging that it has infringed on 31 Acer patents," Chen said.
Chen said the 31 patents alleged to have been infringed involved communications, computer and semiconductor technology.
Chen said he hoped that the two companies could reach a reconciliation through agreements to cross-licence their respective patents.
Lucent is a multibillion-dollar computer and wireless communications firm based in New Jersey.

On July 1, Lucent said it had sued Acer Inc, Acer America Corp, Acer Laboratories Inc of San Jose, California, and Acer Peripherals Labs Inc of Santa Clara, California, alleging violations of eight patents relating to semiconductor manufacturing technologies, speech and video coding and computer display technologies.

Acer, one of the world's leading computer makers, issued an emphatic denial, saying Lucent's patented technologies involved voice communications and voice and video processing technologies that were not directly connected to Acer's main products.
In its initial response to Lucent's lawsuit, Acer said it had been contacted by Lucent to see whether Acer was interested in using some of Lucent's patented technologies.
